accuracy.evidence: Checked for everyday foods from rainforests: cacao native to the Amazon with flowers and pods on the trunk and older branches, 20 to 60 seeds a pod (Britannica 'Cacao'); ferment about 5 to 7 days, sun-dry about a week, roast, grind, add sugar (ICCO processing pages); Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana grow about half or more of world cocoa (ICCO); vanilla is a climbing orchid from Mexico and Central America whose green pods are cured dark brown (Kew); Brazil nut trees reach about 50 m, need large-bodied forest bees to open the hooded flower, fruit poorly alone or in plantations, hold 10 to 25 nuts a fruit and are dispersed by agoutis (Mori and Prance 1990; Kew); bananas descend from South-East Asian forest plants (Perrier et al. 2011). The adult text warns not to claim every banana or bar is rainforest-grown today.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented 'chocolate comes from milk or brown cows' belief (2017 Innovation Center for U.S. Dairy survey, 7% of US adults) with a Milk a brown cow distractor card and a Milk card in the sort; 'vanilla is white' via the vanilla prediction; 'foods grow near home' via apples, carrots and bread in the sort; 'pods hang on twigs' via the cacao prediction; 'any insect pollinates' via a Small fly button; and 'a lone tree fruits fine' via the field start state and prediction.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrainfood is built around this topic's own content: a cacao tree with pods drawn on the trunk that changes picture through pod, open pod with white beans, drying mat, roasting pan and chocolate; four drawn plants (cacao, banana plant, vanilla vine on a tree, giant Brazil nut tree); a Brazil nut scene where the forest, the big bee and the agouti each change what grows. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers by doing: wrong boxes explain where each food's plant grows; the cacao steps only advance in the right order and the picture shows each change; tapping Big bee before growing the forest back fails with 'they live in the forest', so the forest-bee link is found, not told; the agouti only works once nuts exist, showing the life cycle; the lunchbox links it to the child's own food. Done messages then confirm each idea.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: chocolate 'made from milk' (sort and cacao steps), pods 'on thin twigs, like apples' (trunk pods in the picture), vanilla 'white, like the ice cream' (the vanilla vine and why text), and a lone Brazil nut tree 'a tree is a tree' (no nuts until the forest returns). Each step's done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions, each wrong option tagged to its own slip with a specific message: cow (no cow makes chocolate), sugar (taste comes from roasted beans), ground and twig (pods on the trunk), cold (apples and carrots grow in cool places), white (pods dried dark brown, ice cream pale from cream), fly (cannot lift the lid), field (no bees without forest), wind (nut balls too heavy; agoutis bury them), zero (both foods count).

readability.evidence: Family lesson: kid text FK grade 2.5 (limit 5.5) and adult FK 8.6 (limit 10.5) by learn/readability.py. Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Chocolate grows on a tree!'); canvas labels are one to five words; terms like pod, bean, vine and agouti are shown in pictures as they are named.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% overlap with any lesson). Every kid paragraph carries a fact (which foods, how cacao becomes chocolate, vanilla and bananas, why Brazil nuts need forest); the adult paragraphs give curriculum links, processing steps, sources and named mistakes, with a closing lab summary for the grown-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all five teach steps before and after Show me: the food card and both drop boxes are large, the six cacao cards sit in two columns at 48 px high, the four plants switch to a 2 by 2 grid under 520 px with readable names, the Brazil nut action cards and lunchbox tiles stay inside the canvas, and nothing is clipped. Young class gives 56 px buttons under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Rainforest plant and Not from a rainforest, a button per cacao step, a button per plant with 'Banana grows on the banana plant' style labels, Grow the forest back, Small fly, Big bee and Agouti, and a button per lunchbox food. say() updates the canvas aria-label and a polite live region after every action; the walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
